json.title: Liturgy — the whole collection ({format}, version {version})
json.intro: A liturgical collection of the Library: works, editions, texts, passages, templates of the hours and Mass, observances, assignments, rules and calendar profiles — nine kinds of entity that refer to each other by "id". Each text has ONE full wording in its edition and language ("text"); everything that belongs to its performance — verse numbers, pauses (* and †), lines and stanzas, V./R., headings, rubrics, repetitions — is structure next to it, never inside it. The same wording gives two views: continuous (as read, with punctuation and paragraphs) and liturgical (with that structure).
json.rules:
- An "id" that exists (in this collection or built in) changes that entity in place: only the fields named change, a field set to null is cleared, the rest stays. A changed built-in entity becomes this collection's own.
- An unknown "id" creates an entity: then "entity_type" and every field marked required are needed.
- {"id": "…", "remove": true} deletes the entity; a built-in one changed here returns to its default. Nothing else is deleted — entities the document leaves out stay.
- References are ids of this collection or built-in ones; the order in the document does not matter. An id merged into another text still works.
- A division is written as pieces of the wording ("layout": [{"text": "…"}, …]): the pieces must follow the wording in order, with only spaces between them. A piece that does not match stops the import and the preview says where. A division always belongs to one version of its wording: change the "text" and send the division again.
- Identical wordings of the same edition and kind become one text; the other ids remain as "aliases", their sources and divisions are kept. Texts that only begin alike, or where one is the beginning of the other, are listed in the preview as candidates to compare — never merged; a shorter one is marked "possibly_truncated".
- Before saving, everything is checked together: a reference to nothing, a text in another language than its edition, a broken verse range, a stale division, an unsupported execution structure … stop the import, and the preview names each one. Then it is saved in one go — all or nothing — and recorded in the import history.
- What a text still lacks is listed in "missing"; such a text is "incomplete" until it is checked.

top.name: The collection's name (the export writes it; the import ignores it)
top.provenance: Where the texts and changes come from; kept in the import history
top.entities: The entities to add, change or remove

common.entity_type: Which of the nine kinds (sections below); may be left out when changing an existing "id"
common.id: Stable name of the entity in this collection — letters, digits and . _ : - (e.g. "psalm.51.pl"); references use it
common.title: Its name in lists (required for a new entity)
common.status: "draft" (default), "approved" — checked content (a text then needs "complete" and a source) — or "incomplete"
common.metadata: Anything else, as a JSON object — kept, not interpreted
common.revision: Counted by the app on every change; ignored on import
common.remove: true: delete this entity — nothing else is needed

type.canonical_work: A work as such — a psalm, canticle, hymn or reading — independent of any translation; its numbers in each numbering are written out.
type.text_edition: An edition or translation: language, publisher, licence and what the licence permits. Every text belongs to one.
type.text_resource: One actual text in one edition — psalm, canticle, antiphon, hymn, reading, responsory, dialogue, versicle, intercessions, response, prayer, doxology, blessing — as ONE wording ("text") with its structure ("layout", see „Wording and structure").
type.passage_definition: A part of a psalm or canticle by verse ranges (internal verse numbers of its text); it copies nothing. Parts with the same "division" form a named division ("two parts", "Ps 119 — 22 parts") in their "order"; reading the whole text or one division needs no second copy.
type.liturgical_template: The parts (slots) of an hour or of Mass, in order, with where their texts are looked for. Built-in templates exist for every hour and Mass (see „Built in”).
type.calendar_observance: A celebration in a calendar: its date rule, rank, colour and precedence.
type.liturgical_assignment: Which text fills which slot, and when (conditions).
type.liturgical_rule: A rule of a calendar: another date, a transfer, another text in a slot, or a slot left out.
type.calendar_profile: A combination of calendars (e.g. Roman + Poland + a diocese) with time zone and language — chosen when reading.

field.work_type: What the work is, one English word: "psalm", "canticle", "hymn", "reading", "prayer"…
field.numbering_systems: Its number in each numbering, written out — e.g. {"hebrew": 51, "vulgate": 50}; never computed
field.biblical_book_id: The biblical book it belongs to (e.g. "Ps")
field.library_entry_id: The UUID of a Library entry — the book or work this comes from
field.language: Language tag, e.g. "pl-PL"; a text has the language of its edition
field.license: The licence or permission the texts are used under
field.permitted_usage: What the licence permits; without "share" the collection cannot be in a public area
field.resource_type: What the text is, one English word: "psalm", "antiphon" (needed for "antiphon_ref"), "prayer", "reading", "hymn", "responsory"…
field.work_id: The "id" of its work (needed for a psalm)
field.source_citation: Exactly where the text was taken from (needed for "approved")
field.complete: true: the whole text is here — a psalm then needs "expected_verses" and every verse from 1
field.expected_verses: How many verses the whole text has
field.resource_id: The "id" of the full text it cuts from; may be left out when the work in this edition has exactly one text with verses
field.ranges: Verse ranges (see „Parts of entities”); they may not overlap
field.numbering_system: Which numbering the verse numbers follow
field.omitted_verses: Verses inside the ranges that are left out (needs "authority_reference")
field.authority_reference: The norm, book or decision this rests on
field.applicability: When the template applies (conditions, see „Parts of entities”)
field.priority: When several apply, the higher number wins
field.slots: Its parts in order (see „Parts of entities”)
field.precedence_class: Class in the table of precedence: 1 (the Triduum) … 13 (weekdays)
field.date_rule: When it falls (a date rule, see „Parts of entities”)
field.calendar_scope: The calendar it belongs to: "roman", "PL", a diocese, a parish…
field.common_type: The common its missing texts come from
field.first_vespers: true: it begins with First Vespers the evening before
field.replaces: The "id" of an observance whose place it takes
field.proper_references: The ids of its proper texts
field.target_context: When the text is used (conditions, see „Parts of entities”)
field.slot_name: The slot of the template it fills, e.g. "psalmody.1" (see „Built in”)
field.resource_ref: The text or passage used — {"id": "…"} (see „Parts of entities”)
field.antiphon_ref: The "id" of an antiphon (a text with "resource_type": "antiphon") said before and after
field.source_layer: The layer it comes from; a slot looks through the layers in its "source_order"
field.fallback_refs: Texts used when the first is missing (approved, complete, in the same language)
field.conditions: When the rule applies (conditions, see „Parts of entities”)
field.applicable_calendar: The calendar (scope) the rule belongs to
field.coverage: "reviewed" only when someone has checked the calendar for the dates below
field.text: The full wording, once — as it is read, with punctuation; paragraphs separated by a blank line. May be left out when "layout" gives every piece (then it is joined from them)
field.text_version: The version of the wording, counted by the app; every division records the version it was made for
field.layout: The main division as pieces of the wording, see „Wording and structure"
field.layouts: Other attested divisions of the same wording (e.g. an antiphon divided elsewhere), each with "id" — chosen by an assignment
field.performance: The order of performance: who says which unit, repetitions as references to units already written, other texts, rubrics
field.notes: Headings, subtitles, sentences, rubrics and sources shown in the liturgical view only — never part of the wording
field.origin: Reading: the origin line ("From the book of the prophet Isaiah", "From a homily…")
field.incipit: Reading: {"text": "…"} — an incipit of its own — or {"unit": "id"} — the beginning of the wording itself, shown as incipit without being repeated
field.intro_formula: A separate introductory formula of the edition ("Let us pray.", "A reading from…")
field.variants: Attested variants: another ending, another doxology stanza — a unit replaced, optionally under conditions (e.g. the short ending at Terce, Sext, None)
field.response_ref: The assembly's response as its own reusable text (the response of the intercessions, Amen)
field.doxology: Psalm or canticle: "after" — Glory be follows where the slot asks for it; "none" — attested without (e.g. a canticle with its own ending)
field.doxology_ref: Which doxology text (otherwise the doxology of the same edition)
field.variant_group: Texts with the same group are attested alternatives of one another (e.g. hymns offered as a choice)
field.aliases: Ids of identical texts merged into this one — references to them still work
field.missing: What is still missing or inferred and must be checked (codes); filled by the app, an empty list confirms the inferred parts
field.numbering: Which numbering the "label" of verses follows (e.g. "as_printed", "hebrew")
field.division: The named division this part belongs to
field.order: The position of this part within its division
field.on: The version of the text the ranges were made for, set by the app
field.antiphon_layout: Which attested division of the antiphon (its "layouts" id)
field.antiphon_repeat: Where the antiphon returns: "around" (before and after), "before", "after", "strophes" (after each stanza, the Invitatory), "none"
field.main_layout: Which attested division of the main text

builtins.title: Built in
builtins.intro: The app brings a basic calendar and a template for every hour and Mass. Refer to them by "id"; to change one, name its "id" with the fields to change; {"id", "remove": true} returns it to the default. They are not a complete Roman or Polish calendar.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Storage: each entity is one entry of this collection, sealed in the browser with the key of its area; every import adds an entry to the import history. The area decides who reads: its members — everyone only when the area is public and its rule for collections is confirmed.
- In the collection: Resources (each text in the continuous and the liturgical view, with its divisions, references, everything that uses it and its revisions) and Calendar and reading — the liturgical day and the hours and Mass composed when they are read, in either view; print/PDF, the composition as JSON and an HTML file to read offline.
- Elsewhere: a knowledge base (Cogita) that adds the collection under Settings → Sources sees its entities as read-only material — the wording, passages with their verses; other Library collections can refer to them; an AI link that includes the collection carries the exact entities in this format (MCP get_liturgy_library) and the wordings (search_entries).
- The import does not delete what the document leaves out, never fetches texts from outside and writes nothing into Cogita or another collection; in a public area it is refused while an edition lacks "share" in "permitted_usage".

wording.title: Wording and structure
wording.intro: A text has one "text". Its structure is written as units — pieces of that wording in order, with what each one is in the performance. Stored as positions; the export writes the pieces again.
wording.unit: "layout" (and "units" of an attested division) — a list of units:
wording.performance: "performance" — steps in order (each with exactly one of "say", "resource", "rubric"):
wording.notes: "notes" — shown in the liturgical view only:
wording.types: "resource_type": {types}. Psalms, canticles and the doxology are shown in verse lines, hymns in stanzas, everything else as prose with its marks.
wording.checks: Checked: the pieces follow the wording; units neither overlap nor leave text out; ids are unique; steps, notes, incipit and variants point to existing units; a division was made for the current version; ranges of a passage exist in its text.

unit.text: The piece of the wording (exactly as in "text", spaces may differ)
unit.id: Its name, for steps, notes, incipit and variants (e.g. "R", "conclusion")
unit.verse: Internal verse number (1, 2, …) — stable, used by passage ranges
unit.label: The number as printed by the edition ("2a", "116"); a stanza number in a hymn
unit.end: How the unit ends: {values} — mediant shows *, flex shows †; verse, stanza and part break the line
unit.cross: true: a sign of the cross ✠ before it

step.say: Units of this text (ids) — a unit already said is a repetition: the wording is not written again
step.resource: Another text (its id), e.g. the common response or the doxology
step.units: With "resource": only these of its units
step.rubric: A rubric line of the edition

note.at: "start", "end" or the id of the unit it stands before
note.source: Where it comes from (e.g. the source of a sentence)

variant.replaces: The id of the unit it replaces (with the following units of the same kind); absent: the whole text
variant.when: Conditions under which it is used (as in "conditions")

hours.title: How an hour is composed
hours.text:
- A slot takes the text of the best assignment (layers in "source_order", then priority); a passage reads only its verses.
- The antiphon of an assignment ("antiphon_ref", division "antiphon_layout") comes back as "antiphon_repeat" says: {repeats}. When repeated, its mediant is shown as "/".
- Glory be follows a psalm or canticle (and each part of a divided psalm) where the slot or the assignment asks for it ("doxology"), unless the text says "doxology": "none" or the assignment says false. The psalm's own view never shows it.
- A prayer takes the variant whose "when" matches (e.g. the short ending); its conclusion and the Amen stay distinct units; a blessing or dismissal is its own text in its own slot.
- Responsories, dialogues and intercessions follow their "performance"; the common response is said where the steps say.
- The opening dialogue, versicles, the blessing and the dismissal are single reusable texts referred to by assignments.

migration.title: Earlier formats
migration.text:
- Version 1 ("recreatio/liturgy", 1) and the first format ("recreatio.liturgy" 1.0/1.1 with "operations") are read and written as version 2.
- Blocks ("structured_content") become one wording: stanzas and paragraphs as paragraphs, responses as lines; rubric and heading blocks become "notes". " * " and " † " inside a text become unit ends and leave the wording.
- "metadata.performance_markers" ({"at", "mark"} per block) become units: * mediant, † flex, / mediant (shown on repetition), ✢ ✣ a sign of the cross; other attested positions ("recitation_mark_variants") become "layouts".
- Speakers P/K/V become V. (cantor), W/R become R. (all); repeated lines become steps of "performance" instead of a second copy.
- Psalms without verse boundaries get verses inferred from the pauses; hymns get lines from capital letters when their number matches the print — both marked in "missing" until checked.
- Intercessions "A, — B." become introduction, petition and second part; the refrain (refrain_resource_id) becomes "response_ref". Prayers get body, conclusion and Amen; "introduction_formula" becomes "intro_formula". Readings get "origin", "reference", the title as a heading and heading lines that continue into the text as incipit.
- Kinds: psalm_fragment → psalm, gospel_canticle → canticle, intercession_refrain → response, blessing_and_conclusion → blessing, office_rubric → dialog (with speakers) or rubric.
- "metadata" stays unchanged (sources, usages, attested differences). A stored record of version 1 is read as version 2; an import that names it writes it as version 2.
